Maya (eng-platform): Heads-up — we're rolling out a new set of runtime+infra metrics to the Console dashboards next sprint. Need sync on exporters, aggregation windows, and a backfill plan. TL;DR: two tiers (hot/cold), 90d retention for hot, 365d downsampled for cold. Thoughts? :eyes:

Carlos (eng-runtime): +1 to tiers. Can you list the exact metrics? some of these are heavy (KV cache miss traces, token-level latency hist).

Maya (eng-platform): Good call. Starter set: request.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), tokens.generated, kv_cache.hits, kv_cache.misses, model.mem_usage_mb, batch.size, error.rate (per-route). We also want a small set of per-tenant quota counters: quota.consumed_tokens, quota.overage_events.

Priya (eng-sre): For SLO/routing we only need p95 and p99 for latency in the hot tier. Anything token-level should be aggregated server-side to avoid cardinality explosion.

Jasper (eng-ml): Agree. For model.mem_usage_mb we should sample at 1s for hot hosts and 1m for cold aggregated buckets. Also would like to preserve a small rolling window of raw KV miss traces for debugging (not full traces, just proto ids).

Ravi (product-analytics): From analytics POV, we need per-route and per-model daily aggregates for cost attribution. 90d hot retention is fine but we need a nightly batch export to BigQuery for long-term billing joins.

Nadia (eng-platform): Ok — implementation plan proposal: exporters emit raw metrics to metrics-ingest topic with label "tier=hot|cold". Aggregation jobs will do the downsample and materialize to metrics-storage. Backfill: 30-day backfill for hot tier, and 180d backfill for downsampled cold (only counts, p95 estimated).

Eve (eng-infra): Two infra flags: 1) exporter versioning — we need a v2 that adds tier label and low-cardinality tenant_id; 2) retention enforcement at storage layer. Can we avoid a full 180d raw retention? storage costs spike.

Carlos (eng-runtime): Exporter v2 is straightforward. Concern: adding tenant_id increases cardinality massively. Suggest we instead emit hashed_tenant_id with bucketed hash (16 buckets) for routing+privacy, and separate per-tenant quota counters only as aggregated counters (not per-request labels).

Priya (eng-sre): Agreed on hashed buckets to limit series. For quota alerts we rely on aggregated counters by tenant_id stored in a separate compact timeseries (per-minute rollups).

Maya (eng-platform): Example exporter config I had in mind:
```
exporter: 
  metrics: [request.latency_ms, tokens.generated, kv_cache.hits, kv_cache.misses, batch.size]
  labels: [model, route, tier, hashed_tenant_bucket]
  frequency: 10s
```
This would be v2.

Jasper (eng-ml): Can we bump frequency for hot routes to 1s for latency histograms? 10s may smooth p99s.

Nadia (eng-platform): We should avoid 1s for all hosts — maybe have sampling: hot_hosts publish histogram at 1s, others at 10s. Aggregator can merge histograms.

Ravi (product-analytics): For BigQuery export, do you plan to export the full histogram or just pXX summaries? Full histograms are harder to query. I'd prefer daily p50/p95/p99 and token counts plus cost weight.

Eve (eng-infra): Storage note: downsample strategy: keep raw 10s series for 30d, then roll to 1h buckets for 335d. That meets the 365d requirement without huge cost. Backfill is heavy — need to schedule a backfill during low-usage weekend.

Carlos (eng-runtime): Backfill approach: run streaming replay from metrics-topic + archive pulls for missing windows. For historic model.mem_usage_mb we only have sparse samples, so our backfill may need to synthesize p95 using host-level aggregates.

Maya (eng-platform): Ops question — who owns the backfill job? Eng-platform will orchestrate, but we need runtime + infra on-call during the initial run. Proposed window: June 14-15 weekend.

Priya (eng-sre): SRE will standby. We'll require a runbook with clear abort conditions (error budget spike, storage ingestion lag > 3h, exporter version mismatch).

Nadia (eng-platform): UX/Console changes: - New dashboard toggles: view 'hot' vs 'cold' data, link to 'backfill status' job, and per-tenant quota panel (aggregated). Also a rollout flag to enable new metrics per-customer for A/B.

Jasper (eng-ml): One more: add a regression guard — when backfilled metrics change historical p95 by >10% we should fire a regression-check alert to owners (to avoid misleading trend lines).

Ravi (product-analytics): And confirm data contract: nightly export contains columns: date, model, route, tenant_hash_bucket, p50, p95, p99, tokens, cost_estimate. This will be consumed by billing jobs.

Eve (eng-infra): I'll add retention+rollup settings to infra config repo. Will also add a dry-run mode for backfill to estimate storage + time.

metrics-bot: Exporter v2 rollout note: canary to 10% of hosts on Thu (June 6), 50% Fri, full Sat. Backfill flagged for weekend June 14-15.

Maya (eng-platform): Great. Action items: 1) Carlos/Eve: exporter v2 PR + canary plan (due Tue EOD). 2) Nadia/Jasper: aggregator rollup logic + regression guard (due Wed). 3) Priya: runbook + on-call schedule (due Thu). 4) Ravi: BigQuery export schema stub (due Tue). 5) Maya: create Console feature flag + dashboard mock (in flight).

Carlos (eng-runtime): I'll open the PR today and link benchmarks.

Nadia (eng-platform): I'll start the aggregator branch. We should have a sync Thurs 10am to finalize runbook.

Priya (eng-sre): 10am works. I'll add to calendar. :white_check_mark:

Maya (eng-platform): Thanks everyone — logging these in the project board. If anything else comes up, reply here.
